questions.question: What does @Qualifier("upi") on a constructor parameter do?
options: Tells Spring to inject the bean named upi when several beans match the type
Marks the bean as the default
questions.explanation: The qualifier names the exact bean to use when the type alone is ambiguous.

questions.question: What happens at start-up when two beans match the requested type and nothing resolves the tie?
options: Spring stops with an error listing the matching beans
Spring picks the first bean it finds
Spring injects all of them into one field
Spring waits until the first request and then chooses
questions.explanation: Spring will not guess: start-up fails and the error lists the names of the matching beans.

questions.question: PaymentMethod has beans upi, card and walletPayment. PaymentDirectory injects Map<String, PaymentMethod> and prints the keys sorted. What is printed?
questions.explanation: The map keys are the bean names, and sorting them gives card, upi, walletPayment.

questions.question: CheckoutService uses @Qualifier("UPI") but the bean was declared as @Component("upi"). What happens at start-up?
options: Spring matches it ignoring letter case
It fails because no bean named UPI exists
questions.explanation: The qualifier must match the bean name exactly, so a different case finds no bean.

questions.question: A developer relies on a parameter named card to choose the card bean, then renames the parameter to method during a refactor. What is the risk?
options: Spring may now fail with an ambiguity error or choose differently
questions.explanation: Name matching is a fallback that breaks silently on rename; @Qualifier makes the choice explicit.
